title: Consistent error responses
summary: Write a custom DRF exception handler so every error has the same shape.
hints: Keep the first line, response = exception_handler(exc, context). Right after it: if response is None: return None. That lets real bugs become 500 errors.
isinstance(exc, ValidationError) is True only for validation errors. Check it first, because validation errors have no "detail" key.
For every other error, DRF puts the message in response.data["detail"]. Wrap it in str(...) to get plain text.
Build the new body as a dict inside a dict: {"error": {"status": ..., "message": ..., "details": ...}}. Use response.status_code for the status, never a typed number.
Put your dict in response.data = ... and return response. Don't return the dict itself: the tests read response.status_code.

quiz.question: Why give every error the same JSON shape?
options: Clients can write one piece of error-handling code instead of special cases
quiz.explanation: Predictable errors make an API much easier to consume, for frontends, mobile apps and other services alike.

quiz.question: Your handler returns None for an unexpected KeyError. What happens?
options: The exception propagates and Django returns a 500
quiz.explanation: Unexpected errors should become 500s, and in production you log them. Don't dress bugs up as 400s.
